name: Steam methane reforming
aliases: Hydrogen production for refining (SMR with PSA)
principle: Natural gas is desulfurised and reacted with steam over a nickel catalyst in externally fired tubes to make syngas. Water-gas shift converts most of the CO to more hydrogen and CO2, and pressure swing adsorption purifies the hydrogen. Without capture the CO2 is vented, partly in the shifted process gas and partly in the reformer flue gas. Blue hydrogen versions capture the process CO2, the flue gas CO2, or both.

equipment: fired tubular reformer with catalyst tubes

reference_plants.name: Air Products Port Arthur SMR CO2 capture (Valero refinery site)
reference_plants.capacity: about 1 Mt/yr CO2 captured by vacuum swing adsorption from SMR process gas, used for enhanced oil recovery
reference_plants.status: capture began 2013 (first SMR; second planned months later)

source.note: DOE Office of Fossil Energy, 25 January 2013

advantages: Lowest-cost route to hydrogen at today's gas prices in the NETL comparison
Mature, widely licensed, very large single trains
Process CO2 can be captured at moderate cost; flue gas capture lifts total capture
limitations: Unabated SMR emits roughly all feed carbon as CO2
High capture rates need flue gas capture as well as process gas capture
